queries.hook: The wish to understand what these texts teach, and to find in them something steady to lean on.
queries.diagnose: The untrained mind runs like the wind, replaying and imagining; left to itself it becomes its own enemy.
queries.steady: The mind can be trained slowly, by practice and letting go; each time it wanders, it can be gently brought back.
queries.act: Bring the mind back each time it wanders, with practice and letting go; make the mind your friend through steady practice.
queries.story: A story of a student who came to a teacher with questions and was led, step by step, toward the truth.

hook.speaker: Bhartrihari
hook.setting: From 'Worship of Shiva': gratitude for a simple life.
hook.sanskrit: यदेतत्स्वच्छन्दं विहरणमकार्पण्यमशनं सहार्यैः संवासः श्रुतमुपशमैकव्रतफलम् । मनो मन्दस्पन्दं बहिरपि चिरस्यापि विमृशन् न जाने कस्यैष परिणतिरुदारस्य तपसः ॥
hook.line: Freedom, simple food, good company, learning that brings calm: what did I do to deserve this?
hook.translation: This freedom to wander at will, food eaten without humiliation, living among noble people, learning whose only fruit is calm, a mind that stirs only gently even when it looks outward for long: I do not know what generous austerity this is the fruit of.
hook.why: Gratitude for a simple life, and devotion without rivalry between forms of God.

alternates.speaker: Rama
alternates.setting: After the war, Lakshmana finds Rama alone and asks how to cross the sea of confusion.
alternates.sanskrit: एवं सदा जातपरात्मभावनः स्वानन्दतुष्टः परिविस्मृताखिलः । आस्ते स नित्यात्मसुखप्रकाशकः साक्षाद्विमुक्तोऽचलवारिसिन्धुवत् ॥
alternates.line: Content in an inner joy, he becomes like an ocean of still water.
alternates.translation: Always absorbed in the sense of the supreme Self, content in his own joy and forgetting all else, he lives radiating that inner happiness, free, like an ocean of still water.

words.en: one who contemplates the supreme self

alternates.why: Quiet sitting and steady faith carry you until understanding becomes natural.

prasang.title: Sit quietly, keep faith
prasang.summary: Rama describes sitting in a quiet place with the senses at rest until the mind becomes like a still ocean, and tells Lakshmana that until he sees the divine everywhere, devotion keeps it alive in the heart.
prasang.lesson: Quiet sitting and steady faith carry you until understanding becomes natural.

alternates.speaker: Krishna
alternates.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on why even the fulfilled keep working for the world.
alternates.sanskrit: यस्त्वात्मरतिरेव स्यादात्मतृप्तश्च मानवः । आत्मन्येव च सन्तुष्टस्तस्य कार्यं न विद्यते ॥
alternates.line: One who is content and delighted in their own self has nothing left to prove.
alternates.translation: But for the person who delights only in the self, is satisfied with the self, and content in the self alone, there is nothing that must be done.
alternates.why: People copy what you do, not what you say; keep showing up.

prasang.title: Even the wise, even God, act for the world's sake
prasang.summary: The one content in the self has nothing left to gain, yet the wise, like Janaka and Krishna himself, keep working because others follow their example.
prasang.lesson: People copy what you do, not what you say; keep showing up.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on being your own friend and staying steady in honour and insult.
verse.sanskrit: उद्धरेदात्मनाऽऽत्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत् । आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः ॥
verse.line: Be on your own side. Lift yourself up, don't push yourself down. You can be your own friend.
verse.translation: Raise yourself by your own self; do not let yourself sink. For the self alone is the friend of the self, and the self alone is the enemy of the self.
verse.why: You can be your own best friend or worst enemy; choose friend.
verse.misuse: Not 'you're alone, so don't ask for help'. Arjuna himself asks for help; this is about not abandoning yourself.

prasang.title: Lift yourself by yourself; marks of the realised
prasang.summary: Raise yourself by yourself; you are your own friend or enemy. The self-mastered person stays calm in heat and cold, praise and blame, and sees friend and foe alike.
prasang.lesson: You can be your own best friend or worst enemy; choose friend.

verse.meaning: A person must lift themselves up by their own effort and must not let themselves sink. The self is the only friend, and the self is the only enemy. No outside force can do this for you.
verse.for_you: Yesterday you found a quiet mind. Today you lift yourself by your own quiet strength.
verse.try_today: Notice when you lift yourself and when you let yourself sink.
verse.scene_line: You sit quietly, and your own self is the friend who keeps you steady.

verse.speaker: Ram
verse.setting: Ram, describing the monsoon to Lakshman, draws a lesson from ponds filling up.
verse.sanskrit: समिटि समिटि जल भरहिं तलावा। जिमि सदगुन सज्जन पहिं आवा॥ सरिता जल जलनिधि महुँ जोई। होइ अचल जिमि जिव हरि पाई ॥
verse.line: Ponds fill drop by drop. Good qualities gather in a person the same way.
verse.translation: Water gathers bit by bit and fills the ponds, as good qualities come one by one to a good person. River water, reaching the ocean, becomes still, as a soul becomes steady on finding Hari.
verse.why: Nature keeps teaching: steadiness, humility, patience, and saving for the dry season.

prasang.title: Ram's monsoon and autumn lessons
prasang.summary: Waiting out the rains on a mountain, Ram points out lessons to Lakshman in each sight: clouds bow low when full, mountains take the rain as the steady take harsh words, small streams swagger, ponds fill drop by drop, autumn sun dries the puddles as contentment dries greed, and fish panic as the water shrinks.
prasang.lesson: Nature keeps teaching: steadiness, humility, patience, and saving for the dry season.

verse.for_you: This morning, your quiet mind becomes a pond, gathering what is good one drop at a time.
verse.try_today: Notice one small good quality in yourself today, like a drop of water filling a pond.
verse.scene_line: You sit quietly while Ram watches the monsoon fill the ponds with water.

why: the river grows still on reaching the sea
the soul rests on finding Hari

verse.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
verse.setting: Class talk 'Concentration and Breathing', America (notes in CW 6).
verse.line: To me the very essence of education is concentration of mind, not the collecting of facts.
verse.translation: To me the very essence of education is concentration of mind, not the collecting of facts. If I had to do my education over again, and had any voice in the matter, I would not study facts at all. I would develop the power of concentration and detachment, and then with a perfect instrument I could collect facts at will.
verse.why: Train the mind to focus and to let go; both matter.

prasang.title: Concentration and detachment
prasang.summary: All success depends on concentration, but along with it we must build the power to detach, since most suffering comes from a mind stuck on something it cannot let go. If he were educated again, he would train concentration and detachment rather than collect facts.
prasang.lesson: Train the mind to focus and to let go; both matter.

verse.try_today: Notice when your mind collects facts and let it rest in quiet attention instead.
verse.scene_line: You sit quietly while facts wait nearby, ready to be gathered at will.

why: train the instrument, not the store of facts
plan_v3.writer_note: Letting-go teaching for a reader who is building something. Explain it through their own situation and feeling: what is released is the grip that hurts them, never their love, their hope or their work. Never say or imply 'stop caring' or 'your hope is the problem'. Read it after the guard verse, which reassures first.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna teaches Arjuna how to meditate and what a settled mind is like.
verse.sanskrit: शनैः शनैरुपरमेद् बुद्ध्या धृतिगृहीतया । आत्मसंस्थं मनः कृत्वा न किञ्चिदपि चिन्तयेत् ॥
verse.line: Little by little, with patience and steady resolve, settle the mind and let other thoughts go.
verse.translation: Little by little one should come to rest, with understanding held steady; fixing the mind on the self, one should think of nothing else.
verse.why: Moderation and gentle return, again and again, settle the mind.

prasang.title: Meditation in detail
prasang.summary: Krishna describes meditation: moderation in food and sleep, the mind like a lamp in a windless place, bringing the wandering mind back, and feeling others' joy and pain as one's own.
prasang.lesson: Moderation and gentle return, again and again, settle the mind.

verse.for_you: Yesterday you gathered facts. Today you let the mind rest in the self, thinking of nothing else.
verse.try_today: Let a single thought go, then let another go.

prasang.title: Three kinds of food, offering, austerity and giving
prasang.summary: Food, offering, austerity and giving each come in three kinds. Speech should be true, kind and helpful; giving should expect nothing back; effort for show doesn't last.
prasang.lesson: Speak kindly and truly, give without strings, and drop the show.

verse.for_you: Yesterday you let the mind rest in the self. Today you see that calm, gentleness, silence, self-restraint and a clean heart are the discipline of mind itself.
verse.try_today: Notice the silence between your morning thoughts and name it peace.
verse.scene_line: In your quiet mornings, the calm mind becomes the austerity of mind itself.

story.title: Young Uddalaka sits down to meditate and his mind will not stay
story.story_hook: A young sage sat down to meditate and his mind ran off within moments. He kept failing for a long time. Then he tried something different.
story.summary: Uddalaka is young, proud and serious. He longs for a calm mind: 'When will I rest in that stillness? When will my mind stop swinging between liking and disliking?' He sits in meditation in the forest, and his monkey-like mind runs to the objects of the senses.
story.lesson: A restless mind is not overcome by force but by patient return and clear inquiry into what one is.
story.teaser: A young sage sat down to meditate and his mind ran off within moments. He kept failing for a long time. Then he tried something different.
